content.text: The source files reveal specific issues the interview did not resolve: Harbor Point has six sign-ins for a paralegal despite the office-only account; Severn has missing or expired subcontractor coverage evidence; and Larkspur has receipts but no time records for staff who do both restaurant and catering work. I’m checking the larger logs so the follow-up questions can name the affected people and records.

I read all four requested sources, the README, the linked classification guide, and all **34 files across the six employer folders**. No repository files were changed.

The smallest viable solution is a reusable Skill backed by a small Python calculation and validation helper. **Policy clarification is the first gate:** several cases cannot be settled from the guide and interview alone.

**Findings and unresolved decisions**

The [classification guide](https://drive.google.com/file/d/REDACTED/view) permits recorded-time allocation under CG-07, but the interview adds exceptions and requires confirmation of rules outside the guide. We must distinguish source facts, house rules, proposed treatments, and human confirmation.

| Employer | Evidence and preliminary assessment | What remains unresolved |
|---|---|---|
| [Harbor Point Legal](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XcPXqwGvBmVSptPmG0kkAmOzXtLDx_GB) | **Hold acceptance.** Tomas Reyes has six dated sign-ins at Sallowmere Court Condominiums; his payroll is **$64,212.48**. Field notes describe office work and say court appearances/closings are not job sites. | What activity do these entries represent? If they trigger the five-day rule, what is the governing code for this law office? The location name alone cannot decide. |
| [Bay Crest Exteriors](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED) | **Reject the reported split as supported.** Timesheets show eight field workers, all with some roofing work; Teresa Lindqvist has nine site days and **$68,430.90** payroll. The application places seven people under clerical. | Does CG-07 permit proportional roofing/siding allocation, or is there a house exception? How is the governing trade determined for Teresa? Annual wages and hours also require an agreed allocation/rounding method. |
| [Severn Homebuilders](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED) | **Reject the reported split under the interview rule.** Dana Whitcomb has 11 site days and **$59,840.70** payroll; Marissa Gale has exactly four. Tidewater has **$41,155.65** in payments without a listed certificate. Kent Island has **$31,645.65** paid after its listed certificate expires. | Missing proof does not establish uninsured status. Confirm CG-06 treatment, the certificate/payment name mismatch, coverage dates versus work/payment dates, and whether full invoice amounts become payroll. |
| [Patuxent Electric](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED) | **Reject the reported split under the interview rules.** Raymond Dunmore has 214 site days and field duties; his **$118,000.00** office salary would become **$63,700.00** trade payroll. Three workers received $65/day, yielding **$720.00 each** above the $47 allowance. | Kyle Brandt received **$390.00** with zero recorded travel days. Establish its nature and documentation. Confirm that the stated owner/allowance rules govern these cases. |
| [Annapolis Courier](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PGc2b6QTrQ8xRkPqUeQ9aWkR1j6J3QPP) | **Reject the reported split under the interview rule.** Lena Ortiz has 25 weeks with at least two ride-along days, implying **$22,808.75** of whole-week pay moved to T-610. | Lena also has six one-day weeks; Paul Haskins has two. Confirm treatment below the threshold and precedence over CG-07 and the general site-day rule. |
| [Larkspur Lane Bistro](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED) | **Hold acceptance.** Hannah Pryor, Ivan Petrov, and Clara Bose work both catering and restaurant shifts. The application assigns their entire **$114,293.80** to catering. | No time records are supplied. Receipts are not automatically a permitted payroll allocation basis. Confirm the house method and whether it applies to these three employees or a wider payroll pool. Receipts also cover calendar months rather than the exact audit period. |

These are planning assessments, not approved audit allocations.

**Principal risks**

- **Rule precedence:** generic time splitting could contradict the whole-person clerical rule or whole-week dispatcher rule.
- **Evidence limits:** field visits occurred after the audit period; they corroborate duties but cannot establish historical day counts. Owner exclusions are described in business records; election forms are not supplied.
- **False precision:** unsupported certificate matches, receipt ratios, or invented travel days could produce plausible but unjustified cents.
- **Incomplete provenance:** each adjustment and every relied-on record needs an employer confirmation question, including evidence supporting unchanged allocations.
- **Reuse and freshness:** each run must retrieve current employer files and rules. Saved source captures support reproducibility but cannot silently replace fresh retrieval.
- **Session evidence:** Entire reports enabled for Codex, but its listed session is marked `exited`. That does not yet prove capture of a future submitted revision; verification belongs in the first and final gates.

**Bounded implementation plan**

Scope: Markdown/CSV sources as supplied, one-employer and six-employer execution, exact required outputs, and a new-employer rerun. No rates, premium calculations, website, database, or automated stakeholder contact.

| Gate | Work and model allocation | Verification and stop condition |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — Evidence and policy agreement** | Astra High owns rule precedence and unresolved decisions. A bounded Sol 6.1 Medium task inventories source schemas and maps requirements to checks. Record ownership and status in `PROJECT-TRACKER.md`. | All source files accounted for; policy decisions tied to original interview evidence; remaining unknowns explicitly classified as proposed or blocked; retrieval and session capture demonstrated. **Owner accepts policy and output behavior before implementation.** |
| **2 — Small reusable implementation** | Astra High owns policy integration. Sol 6.1 Medium implements retrieval/normalization and deterministic arithmetic in separate owned files; use High for difficult debugging only. Create `skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md`, focused supporting files, and one small runner. | Test four/five site days, one/two route days, owner exclusion/replacement, allowance boundaries and zero-day inconsistency, certificate gaps, mixed work, and cent conservation. Missing or contradictory evidence must produce visible open items, never silent approval. **Owner reviews one simple case and one disputed case.** |
| **3 — Six-employer outputs and reuse** | Sol 6.1 Medium generates and validates outputs and README instructions. Astra High integrates decisions and proposed call priorities. | Six exact CSV filenames and column order; positive allocations only; two decimals; code-description paragraph IDs; employee/payment adjustments reconcile to totals; every relied-on record and adjustment has a confirmation question. Run a synthetic new employer and a changed-source rerun to expose hardcoding or stale reuse. **Owner accepts the complete draft package.** |
| **4 — Completion review** | One integrated Astra High review, as required by `ORCHESTRATION.md`. | Verify requirements, unresolved-item visibility, repeatable commands, Skill validation/security scan, and real capture records associated with the submitted revision. Fix material findings and rerun affected checks. **Stop for final acceptance.** |

Use Python `Decimal` for money and explicit date/employee joins. Keep language-model interpretation in a reviewable decision record; generate the CSVs, report, and questions from the same reconciled allocation data. The runner should accept source locations, not employer-specific answers.

The model allocation follows [ORCHESTRATION.md](/home/mike/ch03-premium-audit/ORCHESTRATION.md): **Astra High leads; Sol 6.1 handles bounded work; no Extra High.** This also matches the official positioning of Astra for demanding reasoning and Sol for balancing capability and cost. [OpenAI model documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)

**Two stakeholder follow-ups maximum**

The [README interview rule](/home/mike/ch03-premium-audit/README.md) requires you to conduct the interview yourself. These are preparation topics for your own questions; no stakeholder contact has been made.

1. **One consolidated policy-and-evidence follow-up with Nadia.** Bring the six cases above. Resolve Harbor’s actual site activity/code; Bay’s mixed-trade and governing-code rules; Severn’s coverage/name/date/invoice treatment; Patuxent’s $390 discrepancy; Courier’s one-day weeks; and Larkspur’s allocation method. Confirm precedence and approval status of the four already-stated house rules. Request any specifically relevant missing records in this same conversation.

2. **Reserve one final confirmation follow-up.** Present the calculated adjustments, remaining open items, and two recommended employer calls. Confirm what may appear in provisional CSVs when an issue remains unresolved, who signs off, and the exact Friday deadline. Skip this follow-up if the first resolves everything.

My provisional call priorities are **Bay Crest** for the breadth of unsupported clerical allocation, and **Severn** for the combination of employee reclassification and subcontractor coverage gaps. That ranking uses classification uncertainty and affected payroll—not an unverified premium estimate.

Stopped for your review, as requested. No implementation has begun.

Package this as IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md, and start a PROJECT-TRACKER.md file that keeps track cumulative agent time, and tokens, updated when a push occurs, with an estimate of 4 hours, and 50 million tokens respectfully. The tracker can also keep track of project process/current context, but keep it concise as a rule.

I’ll save the plan as `IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` and create a concise `PROJECT-TRACKER.md` with estimates of 4 agent-hours and 50 million tokens. I’ll specify that cumulative usage is updated at each push, with unavailable measurements marked as unknown.
